This session did NOT redo any ceremony — it read sprint 5's plan, which sequences committed-core items in priority order specifically to stop long-running items (a board session, an unconverged PR) from zeroing out a sprint's throughput again (per #1445, filed after sprints 3 and 4 both did exactly that). Per that sequencing, this session took sprint 5's item #1 (#442 — guard-commit/record-green resolve PROJECT_DIR to the outer main checkout instead of a worktree-isolated session's own worktree root, making the commit gate flaky-deny whenever the main repo is busy with concurrent agents) and delegated it to the implementer agent via TDD, NOT in an isolated worktree (shared checkout — the agent's own branch checkout was momentarily visible in `git status`/`git branch` mid-session, as in a prior session's note; harmless, just disorienting to watch).

Result: PR #1512 opened (branch `fix/442-worktree-project-dir` -> `main`, `Closes #442`), full suite green (361/361 including 4 new regression assertions), mergeable, not yet reviewed. Root cause: `command_target_dir()` in `hooks/lib/common.sh` only overrides `PROJECT_DIR` when the command text carries an explicit `cd`/`git -C` prefix; with no such prefix (the normal shape for an in-worktree commit, since the Bash tool's cwd is already the worktree) it fell through to the session-wide `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, which stays pointed at the outer checkout for a worktree-isolated session's whole lifetime. Fix: fall back to the event's own reported `cwd` (`_project_from_input`) before falling back to `PROJECT_DIR` when no explicit cd/-C is present. Session left the checkout back on `main`, clean, after PR #1512 was pushed.
